title: Two-stage OTA, cascode compensation
description: The Ahuja (cascode) variant of the two-stage Miller OTA: the compensation cap $C_c$ returns to a low-impedance cascode node instead of directly across the second stage. Routing the compensation current through the common-gate cascode blocks the feedforward path, so the right-half-plane zero that plagues plain Miller compensation is removed and the pole-splitting is better damped — for the same GBW the phase margin comes almost entirely from the second pole. The stage structure mirrors the plain Miller OTA (stage-1 input pair + mirror load, stage-2 common source + load); the added cascode devices carry the stage-1 branch currents, and the one on the output side provides the node $C_c$ returns through. The first stage is drawn with both of its sides, because they do not sit at the same voltages. On the diode side the mirror device's drain is its own gate, one diode drop below the supply, and the cascode and the input device stack under that node. On the output side the mirror's output device and the cascode share a drain that is the second stage's gate, so it sits one second-stage $V_{GS}$ below the supply instead. The stage is drawn at rest, as the feedback around the amplifier holds it: the stage-1 output sits at the second stage's gate, and the two inputs sit apart by whatever offset that takes. The currents are stated the way the circuit sets them: the bias reference is programmed with $I_1$, the tail device shares that reference's gate and width, the two input devices are one width and carry what the tail delivers between them, each its own share, and the second stage carries what its load delivers: the load is a second mirror output of the same reference, on its gate at $K_2$ times its width, so the stage-2 current is $K_2 I_1$ less that mirror's drain-voltage error, and the second-stage device is handed it. The mirror's output device takes its diode-side partner's width and gate and carries what the table gives at its own drain voltage. The pair is sized on its output side, and the share is solved so that the currents at the stage-1 output balance: the output-side cascode passes up exactly what the mirror's output device returns. The output-side cascode takes the diode-side cascode's width and carries the current of the input device below it, and the node under it is solved: it sits where that cascode needs the gate voltage the two cascodes share. The tail node, the share and that node read each other, so the engine settles the three together by repeated one-unknown searches. Wherever the two levels differ, the two input devices need different gate-source voltages for their currents, and the systematic-offset row reports that difference directly. Entered from the COMMON MODE like the 5T: the input pair's tail node is solved so the produced $CM_{in}$, the tail node plus the mean of the two gate-source voltages, equals $CM_{dc}$. The pole and phase-margin rows are ESTIMATE-grade small-signal approximations; the simulator owns stability sign-off. On the demo NMOS table the polarity-inverted devices keep their sign params at +1.

params.name: CL
params.note: output load capacitance

params.name: Av_target
params.note: two-stage DC gain target: 100 (40 dB), a 1 % static error in unity feedback, is a loose floor for a general-purpose two-stage amplifier, which commonly reaches 60 to 80 dB. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: GBW_target
params.note: unity-gain bandwidth target into the 5 pF load: a few megahertz is the range of a general-purpose two-stage amplifier biased at tens of microamps. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: PM_target
params.note: phase-margin target; cascode comp removes the RHP zero so a higher target is realistic. Estimate-grade

params.name: SR_target
params.note: slew-rate target: 5 V/us moves a 1 V step in 200 ns, in keeping with a few-megahertz general-purpose amplifier driving 5 pF. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: C1_est
params.note: stage-1 output node cap (stage-2 gate + parasitics + wiring); refine from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis This sheet carries NO containment edges; see the single-stage OTAs for the pattern.

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the input pair's tail node. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke. An end of the range where the relation does not evaluate — on a process whose PMOS diode eats most of the rail, the top of the range, where the pair has no drain-source voltage under the mirror diode drop — is stepped inward silently, and the searched range is reported only if the search then fails. This variant stacks the cascode in the same budget, which is why V_casc is kept low; raising gm_id_ld1 for a smaller diode drop is the other knob that gives the input devices room

params.name: Cc
params.note: cascode compensation cap: sets the dominant pole and GBW = gm1/(2*pi*Cc)

params.name: I1
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on the sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 and the second-stage load K2:1 through the shared gate, and each delivers it less its own drain-voltage error (the tail node normally sits below the reference's diode drop, the output above it); the slew limits and the supply current are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: K2
params.note: mirror ratio of the second-stage load, as a width ratio: the load sits on the bias reference's gate at K2 times its width and at its length, so it is a mirror output of that reference and the device that sets the stage-2 current. It delivers K2 times I1 less its drain-voltage error — its drain is the output, above the reference's diode drop — and the second-stage device carries what it delivers. Raising it buys stage-2 slew and a higher second pole for supply current

params.name: out_share
params.note: the share of the tail current the pair's output-side device carries at rest — solved, not set. The stage-1 output is a high-impedance node, held where it is by the feedback around the amplifier, so in the resting circuit the current the output-side cascode passes up from the input device below it is exactly the current the mirror's output device returns: the engine searches for the share at which the two are equal, the current law at the stage-1 output. The diode-side device carries the rest, so the two add up to what the tail delivers by construction. It is searched between 0.01 and 0.99, a share of the tail current that leaves each device some of it; the stored value is never read

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device and the second-stage load inherit through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node and output swing at the load. Set weak, at 14, because the tail node sits only about 0.2 V above ground on a sky130 tt realization: at 10 the tail device leaves saturation at the slow corner when warm

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference, the tail device and the second-stage load, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks each mirror's drain-voltage error and the load's output conductance

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion, set on the output-side device; the diode-side device copies its width and carries the rest of the tail current

params.name: gm_id_ld1
params.note: stage-1 mirror-load inversion, set on the diode side and inherited by the output side through the shared gate

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode device inversion, set on the diode-side cascode; the output-side cascode takes its width and its gate

params.name: gm_id_s2
params.note: stage-2 device inversion

params.name: V_out2
params.note: stage-2 output DC level. The stage-2 device and its current-source load meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here

params.name: V_casc
params.note: drain-source voltage of the diode-side cascode, whose drain is the mirror node. Stated at this design point, and kept low: the mirror's diode drop, this cascode and the input device under it share what is left above the tail node, and on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table that is about 0.6 V, so at 0.4 V the input devices sat in triode. Where the design is held fixed (another process condition), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max: from 0.1 V up to the 0.6 V the stack can give it, which keeps the search starting where the input device under it still has a drain-source voltage at the cold slow corner

params.name: V_casco
params.note: drain-source voltage of the output-side cascode, whose drain is the stage-1 output and whose source is the low-impedance node Cc returns through. Solved rather than set: the two cascodes share one gate, so this is searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the output-side cascode's gate voltage equals the diode-side cascode's. An end of the range where the relation does not evaluate — the max, where it leaves the input device under this cascode no drain-source voltage — is stepped inward silently, and the searched range is reported only if the search then fails

params.name: out_sign
params.note: vds sign of the stage-2 device table: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

params.name: ld1o_sign
params.note: vds sign of the table the stage-1 mirror's output device reads: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis. The diode side needs none — its drain follows its own gate in whichever convention its table uses. Read both sides of the mirror from the same table: the gate voltage they share is passed in that table's convention

params.name: vos_sys_target
params.note: systematic input offset budget. The offset is set by how far the second stage's gate-source voltage sits from the stage-1 mirror's diode drop, referred to the input through the first-stage gain, so this is the budget for leaving the two unequal: 50 mV between them at a first-stage gain of 50 is 1 mV

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_1$ flows into — the one device on the sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device and the second-stage load need to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with $V_{tail}$ as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It has to stay saturated, and it leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Stage-1 mirror-load device, diode side
doc.description: The diode-connected side of the stage-1 current-mirror load. It carries the current of the input device and the cascode below it — what the tail delivers less the output-side device's share — and its drain is its gate, so it sits one $V_{GS}$ below the supply whatever the stage-1 output does. That gate is the mirror node: this device's width and gate voltage are what the output side copies.

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device carrying the full stage-2 current — what its load delivers — at the output DC level; its gm sets the second pole and its gate cap dominates the stage-1 output node.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-1 mirror-load device, output side
doc.description: The output side of the stage-1 mirror load, on the diode side's gate at the diode side's width. Its drain is the stage-1 output, and that node is the second stage's gate, so this device sits one second-stage $V_{GS}$ below the supply rather than one diode drop. Its current is read off the table at that drain voltage rather than typed: wherever the two levels differ it is not the diode side's current, and the difference is the larger part of the systematic offset the sheet reports. Its output conductance loads the first-stage gain.

params.name: Wx
params.note: the diode side's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgsx
params.note: the diode side's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share, in the sign convention of the diode side's table

params.name: vx
params.note: the supply down to the stage-1 output, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device, output side
doc.description: The input device on the stage-1 output side, sized at its share of what the tail delivers. The pair's two devices share a width and a source; the share is set by the current law at the stage-1 output. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain is the source of the output-side cascode, which holds it within a few millivolts of the diode-side device's drain. Its width is what its partner on the diode side copies; its gate-source voltage differs from its partner's by the input offset that holds the stage-1 output where it is.

params.name: vx
params.note: from the output-side cascode's source down to the tail node

params.name: vsbx
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device, diode side
doc.description: The input device on the mirror's diode side, in one branch with the cascode and the diode-connected mirror device above it. It is the output-side device's width, carrying the rest of what the tail delivers: a matched pair is one width, so its width is copied, and its current is given, which makes this a width-and-current sizing — the table is inverted at that current density for the gate-source voltage it takes. Its source sits at the tail node like its partner's, and its drain sits one cascode drop BELOW the mirror node, so its drain-source voltage is what is left after both the mirror diode drop and V_casc. Wherever its current or its drain differs from its partner's, its gate-source voltage differs too, and that difference is the input offset the sheet reports.

params.name: Wx
params.note: the output-side device's width — the pair is matched

params.name: Ix
params.note: what the tail delivers less the output-side device's share

params.name: vx
params.note: from the diode-side cascode's source down to the tail node

params.name: vsbx
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Cascode device, diode side
doc.description: The common-gate cascode in the diode-side branch, between the input device and the mirror node, carrying the current of the input device below it. It is sized here for its inversion level; its width and its gate voltage are what the output-side cascode shares.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

params.name: vsbx
params.note: the source stands on the input device's drain node, not the bulk

doc.title: Compensation cascode device, output side
doc.description: The common-gate cascode in the output-side branch, between the input device and the stage-1 output; the compensation cap returns to its low-impedance source, so the feedforward path (and the RHP zero) is blocked. It is the diode-side cascode's width on the diode-side cascode's gate, and it carries the current of the input device below it. Its drain sits at the second stage's gate rather than at the mirror node, so its source settles a little away from the diode-side cascode's — the node this sheet solves.

params.name: Wx
params.note: the diode-side cascode's width — the two are matched

params.name: vx
params.note: from the stage-1 output down to this device's source

params.name: vsbx
params.note: the source stands on the output-side input device's drain node, not the bulk

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting: the tail node plus the mean of the two input devices' gate-source voltages, the level the two inputs sit about. It rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: V_mir
equations.note: the stage-1 mirror node — the diode side's drain and the gate the two mirror devices share, one diode drop below the supply

equations.name: V1
equations.note: stage-1 output DC. Derived, not typed: this node is the second stage's gate, so it sits one second-stage gate-source voltage below the supply (abs() keeps both table conventions working). It is the drain of the mirror's output device and of the output-side cascode, and it is not the mirror node: the two levels differ by the difference between the second stage's gate-source voltage and the mirror's diode drop

equations.name: gm1
equations.note: stage-1 transconductance into the stage-1 output node. Each input device turns half the differential input into current: the diode-side half reaches the output through the mirror, whose current gain is its output device's $g_m$ over its diode device's, and the output-side half arrives through its cascode. It is one input device's $g_m$ where the two sides sit at the same levels

equations.name: gm2
equations.note: stage-2 transconductance sets the second pole

equations.name: gm_casc
equations.note: transconductance of the output-side cascode, the one Cc returns through (sets the impedance of that node)

equations.name: GBW
equations.note: compensated unity-gain bandwidth (input gm into the compensation cap)

equations.name: p2
equations.note: non-dominant pole ESTIMATE; cascode compensation both removes the RHP zero and pushes this pole out — refine C1_est from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

equations.name: PM
equations.note: ESTIMATE: only the second-pole phase lag remains because the cascode blocks the feedforward RHP zero. Small-signal approximation — the simulator owns stability sign-off

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the smaller slew limit: the current the tail device delivers charging Cc, or the current the second-stage load delivers charging CL

equations.name: Av1
equations.note: stage-1 gain into the output conductances of the pair's output-side device and of the mirror's output device. The cascode above the input device raises the resistance looking down from the stage-1 output; this row does not count that, so it understates the gain

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the resistance the amplifier presents at its output — stage two's own output conductance in parallel with its load device's. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av2
equations.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

equations.name: Av
equations.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

equations.name: vos_sys
equations.note: input-referred systematic offset — the difference of the two input devices' gate-source voltages at rest, read directly: the input offset the feedback holding the output, and with it the second stage's gate, has to apply. The mirror's output device sits at the second stage's gate voltage instead of the mirror's diode drop, so it returns a different current than its diode side carries, and the output-side input device has to carry that current instead of an even share; the cascodes hold the two input devices' drains within millivolts of each other, so the currents are the larger part of it. It is zero when the second stage's gate-source voltage equals the mirror's diode drop — the classic condition that the second-stage device and the mirror devices run at one current density

equations.name: cgg2
equations.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the current the tail device delivers plus the current the second-stage load delivers. The reference branch that programs the tail and the load is shared bias infrastructure, typically one reference feeding several stages, and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target
the worse of the two slew limits meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target
ESTIMATE-grade phase margin (no RHP zero term); the simulator owns the real stability sign-off

checks.lhs: min(V_mir - V_casc - V_tail - in__vdsat, V1 - V_casco - V_tail - ino__vdsat)
checks.note: each input device has what is left under its cascode, and this watches whichever has less room. Trips when the tail node is pushed so high that device runs out of drain-source voltage — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less of the supply above it

the systematic input offset stays inside its budget. The stage-1 output sits at the second stage's gate, V1 = VDD - |vgs_s2|, while the mirror node sits at VDD - |vgs_ld1|, and the offset grows with the distance between the two — the classic W/L-ratio condition. Retune gm_id_s2 or gm_id_ld1 until the two gate-source voltages agree and the offset falls to zero
